params.name: count_only
params.description: Return only {"count": N} without records or pagination. Useful for fetching the total count asynchronously after an initial fast query.

params.name: include_count
params.description: Deprecated. COUNT is now always included by default.

params.name: limit
params.description: Number of results to return per page.

params.name: offset
params.description: The initial index from which to return the results.

params.name: schema
params.description: The schema ID that this record belongs to.

params.name: skip_count
params.description: Skip the COUNT(*) query. When true, the response omits the X-Total-Count header and the Link rel="last" header. Useful for faster responses on large result sets.

items.docs:
List records for the given schema ID. Takes optional pagination parameters
`limit` and `offset`, as well as an optional query filter `q`.

The response will be a list of record objects.

**On the command line:**

```bash
blind records list --schema "<schema-id>"
```

#

Create a new record with an already encrypted payload. This is the non-porcelain
endpoint. If you want to create a new record with plaintext data, use the
`record create` porcelain command or the `records ingest` command with a proxy.

The response will be the newly created record object.

**On the command line:**

```bash
blind records create --data encrypted-record.json
```

params.name: id
params.description: An array of record IDs to be deleted.

items.docs:
Delete multiple records by their IDs.

The response will be a 204 No Content if successful.

**On the command line:**

```bash
blind records bulk-destroy --id "<record-id>" --id "<record-id>"
```

params.name: id
params.description: A unique value identifying this record.

items.docs:
Retrieve a record by its ID.

The response will be the record object.

**On the command line:**

```bash
blind records retrieve --id "<record-id>"
```
